3.9.d: अनश्नन् संहिता सहस्रम् अधीयीत । ब्रह्मभूतो विरजो ब्रह्म भवति ।
3.9.e: If, fasting, he recites the Saṃhitā one thou-sand (times), he becomes one with Brahman, resplendent like Brahman (and) Brahman (itself).

3.9.s: saṃvatsaraṃ bhaikṣaṃ prayuñjāno divyaṃ cakṣur labhate |
3.9.d: संवत्सरं भैक्षं प्रयुञ्जानो दिव्यं चक्षुर् लभते ।
3.9.e: If he subsists during a year on food obtained by begging, he gains (the power of) supernatural vision.

3.9.s: ṣaṇ māsān yāvakabhakṣaś caturo māsān udakasaktubhakṣo dvaumāsau phalabhakṣo māsam abbhakṣo dvādaśarātraṃ vāprāśnan kṣipram antardhīyate jñātīn punāti saptāvarān sapta pūrvān ātmānaṃpañcadaśaṃ paṅktiṃ ca punāti |
3.9.d: षण् मासान् यावकभक्षश् चतुरो मासान् उदकसक्तुभक्षो द्वौमासौ फलभक्षो मासम् अब्भक्षो द्वादशरात्रं वाप्राश्नन् क्षिप्रम् अन्तर्धीयते ज्ञातीन् पुनाति सप्तावरान् सप्त पूर्वान् आत्मानंपञ्चदशं पङ्क्तिं च पुनाति ।
3.9.e: If during six months he subsists on barley-gruel, during four months on water and barley-flour, during two months on fruit, (and) during one month on water, or performs K ri k kh ra penances of twelve days, he (obtains the power of) suddenly disappearing, and sanctifies seven descendants, seven ancestors, and himself as the fifteenth, and (any) company (of Brāhmaṇas) which he may enter.

3.9.s: tām etāṃ devaniśrayaṇīty ācakṣate |
3.9.d: ताम् एतां देवनिश्रयणीत्य् आचक्षते ।
3.9.e: They call that the ladder of the gods.

3.9.s: etayā vai devā devatvam agacchann ṛṣaya ṛṣitvam |
3.9.d: एतया वै देवा देवत्वम् अगच्छन्न् ऋषय ऋषित्वम् ।
3.9.e: By means of that the gods reached their divine station and the sages the position of Ri shis.

3.9.s: tasya ha vā etasya yajñasya trividha evārambhakālaḥprātaḥsavane mādhyaṃdine savane brāhme vāpararātre |
3.9.d: तस्य ह वा एतस्य यज्ञस्य त्रिविध एवारम्भकालःप्रातःसवने माध्यंदिने सवने ब्राह्मे वापररात्रे ।
3.9.e: The periods for beginning this sacrifice, forsooth, are three, the time of the morning libation, the time of the midday libation, and the last part of the night, (the Muhūrta) sacred to Brahman.

3.9.s: taṃ vā etaṃ prajāpatiḥ saptarṣibhyaḥ provāca saptarṣayomahājajñave mahājajñur brāhmaṇebhyaḥ | brāhmaṇebhyaḥ |
3.9.d: तं वा एतं प्रजापतिः सप्तर्षिभ्यः प्रोवाच सप्तर्षयोमहाजज्ञवे महाजज्ञुर् ब्राह्मणेभ्यः । ब्राह्मणेभ्यः ।
3.9.e: Pra g āpati, forsooth, proclaimed this (rite) to the seven Ri shis, the seven Ri shis to Mahā g a g ñ u, and Mahā g a g ñ u to the Brāhmaṇas.

3.10.e: The law of castes and of orders has been declared.

3.10.s: atha khalv ayaṃ puruṣo yāpyena karmaṇā mithyā vā caratyayājyaṃ vā yājayaty apratigrāhyasya vā pratigṛhṇāty anāśyānnasyavānnam aśnāty acaraṇīyena vā carati |
3.10.d: अथ खल्व् अयं पुरुषो याप्येन कर्मणा मिथ्या वा चरत्ययाज्यं वा याजयत्य् अप्रतिग्राह्यस्य वा प्रतिगृह्णात्य् अनाश्यान्नस्यवान्नम् अश्नात्य् अचरणीयेन वा चरति ।
3.10.e: Now, indeed, man (in) this (world is polluted) by a vile action or acts wrongly, (e.g.) sacrifices for men. unworthy to offer a sacrifice, accepts presents from those whose gifts ought not to be accepted, eats the food of those whose food ought not to be eaten, (and) practises what is forbidden.

3.10.s: tatra prāyaścittaṃ kuryān na kuryād iti mīmāṃsante |
3.10.d: तत्र प्रायश्चित्तं कुर्यान् न कुर्याद् इति मीमांसन्ते ।
3.10.e: They are in doubt if he shall perform a penance for such (a deed) or if he shall not do it.
(They declare that he shall not do it) because the deed does not perish.
(The correct opinion is) that he shall perform (a penance).
It is declared in the Veda, 'Let him offer a Punastoma; (those who offer it, may) again come to (partake of) the libations of Soma.'

3.10.s: athāpy udāharanti | sarvaṃ pāpmānaṃ tarati taratibrahmahatyāṃ yo 'śvamedhena yajata iti |
3.10.d: अथाप्य् उदाहरन्ति । सर्वं पाप्मानं तरति तरतिब्रह्महत्यां यो ऽश्वमेधेन यजत इति ।
3.10.e: He who offers a horse-sacrifice conquers all sin, he effaces the guilt of the murder of a Brāhmaṇa.'
Moreover, 'He who is being accused (of a heinous crime) shall perform an Agnishṭut sacrifice.'

3.10.s: tasya niṣkrayaṇāni japas tapo homa upavāso dānam |
3.10.d: तस्य निष्क्रयणानि जपस् तपो होम उपवासो दानम् ।
3.10.e: Reciting the Veda, austerity, a sacrifice, fasting, giving gifts are the means for expiating such (a blamable act).

3.10.s: upaniṣado vedādayo vedāntāḥ sarvacchandaḥsu saṃhitā madhūnyaghamarṣaṇam atharvaśiro rudrāḥ puruṣasūktaṃ rājanarauhiṇe sāmanībṛhadrathaṃtare puruṣagatir mahānāmnyo mahāvairājaṃ mahādivākīrtyaṃjyeṣṭhasāmnām anyatamaṃ bahiṣpavamānaḥ kūśmāṇḍyaḥ pāvamānyaḥ sāvitrī ceti pāvanāni |
3.10.d: उपनिषदो वेदादयो वेदान्ताः सर्वच्छन्दःसु संहिता मधून्यघमर्षणम् अथर्वशिरो रुद्राः पुरुषसूक्तं राजनरौहिणे सामनीबृहद्रथंतरे पुरुषगतिर् महानाम्न्यो महावैराजं महादिवाकीर्त्यंज्येष्ठसाम्नाम् अन्यतमं बहिष्पवमानः कूश्माण्ड्यः पावमान्यः सावित्री चेति पावनानि ।
3.10.e: The purificatory (texts are), the Upanishads, the initial (verses) of the Vedas, the ends of the Vedas (vedāntas), the Saṃhitās of all the Vedas, (the Anuvākas called) Madhu, (the hymn of) Aghamarshaṇa, the Atharvaśiras, (the Anuvākas called the) Rudras, the Purusha hymn, the two Sāmans (called) Rā g ina and Rauhiṇeya, the B ri hat (Sāman) and the Rathantara, the Purushagati (Sāman), the Mahānāmnīs, the Mahāvairā g a (Sāman), the Mahādivākīrtya (Sāman), any of the G yesh th a Sāmans, the Bahishpavamāna Sāman, the Kūshmāṇd īs, the Pāvamānīs, and the Sāvitrī.

3.10.s: upasannyāyena payovratatā śākabhakṣatā phalabhakṣatāmūlabhakṣatā prasṛtiyāvako hiraṇyaprāśanaṃ ghṛtaprāśanaṃsomapānam iti medhyāni |
3.10.d: उपसन्न्यायेन पयोव्रतता शाकभक्षता फलभक्षतामूलभक्षता प्रसृतियावको हिरण्यप्राशनं घृतप्राशनंसोमपानम् इति मेध्यानि ।
3.10.e: To live on milk alone, as if one were fasting, to eat vegetables only, to eat fruit only, (to live on) gruel prepared of a handful of barley-grains, to eat gold, to eat clarified butter (are the modes of subsistence) which purify.

3.10.s: sarve śiloccayāḥ sarvāḥ sravantyaḥ saritaḥ puṇyā hradāstīrthāny ṛṣiniketanāni goṣṭhakṣetrapariṣkandā iti deśāḥ |
3.10.d: सर्वे शिलोच्चयाः सर्वाः स्रवन्त्यः सरितः पुण्या ह्रदास्तीर्थान्य् ऋषिनिकेतनानि गोष्ठक्षेत्रपरिष्कन्दा इति देशाः ।
3.10.e: All mountains, all rivers, holy lakes, bathing-places, the dwellings of Ri shis, cowpens, (holy) plains and temples of the gods (are) places (which destroy sin)

3.10.s: ahiṃsā satyam astainyaṃ savaneṣūdakopasparśanaṃguruśuśrūṣā brahmacaryam adhaḥśayanam ekavastratānāśaka ititapāṃsi |
3.10.d: अहिंसा सत्यम् अस्तैन्यं सवनेषूदकोपस्पर्शनंगुरुशुश्रूषा ब्रह्मचर्यम् अधःशयनम् एकवस्त्रतानाशक इतितपांसि ।
3.10.e: Abstention from injuring living beings, truthfulness, abstention from theft (or unrighteously appropriating anything), bathing in the morning, at noon, and in the evening, obedience towards Gurus, continence, sleeping on the ground, dressing in one garment only, and abstaining from food (are the various kinds of) austerity.

3.10.s: hiraṇyaṃ gaur vāso 'śvo bhūmis tilā ghṛtam annam iti deyāni |
3.10.d: हिरण्यं गौर् वासो ऽश्वो भूमिस् तिला घृतम् अन्नम् इति देयानि ।
3.10.e: Gold, a cow, a dress, a horse, land, sesamum, clarified butter, and food (are) the gifts.

3.10.s: saṃvatsaraḥ ṣaṇmāsāś catvāras trayo dvāv ekaścaturviṃśatyaho dvādaśāhaḥ ṣaḍahas tryaho 'horātra ekāha itikālāḥ |
3.10.d: संवत्सरः षण्मासाश् चत्वारस् त्रयो द्वाव् एकश्चतुर्विंशत्यहो द्वादशाहः षडहस् त्र्यहो ऽहोरात्र एकाह इतिकालाः ।
3.10.e: A year, six months, four (months), three (months), two (months), one (month), twenty-four days, twelve days, six days, three days, a day and a night, (and) one day are the periods (for penances).
These (acts) may be optionally performed if no (particular penance) has been prescribed,
(Viz.) for great crimes difficult (penances) and for trivial faults easy ones.
The K ri k kh ra and the Atik ri k kh ra, as well as the K āndrāyaṇa, are penances for all (offences).

4.1.s: prāyaścittāni vakṣyāmo nānārthāni pṛthakpṛthak | teṣuteṣu ca doṣeṣu garīyāṃsi laghūni ca |
4.1.d: प्रायश्चित्तानि वक्ष्यामो नानार्थानि पृथक्पृथक् । तेषुतेषु च दोषेषु गरीयांसि लघूनि च ।
4.1.e: We will separately explain the various penances for the several offences, both heavier and lighter ones.

4.1.s: yady atra hi bhaved yuktaṃ tad hi tatraiva nirdiśet | bhūyobhūyo garīyaḥsu laghuṣv alpīyasas tathā |
4.1.d: यद्य् अत्र हि भवेद् युक्तं तद् हि तत्रैव निर्दिशेत् । भूयोभूयो गरीयःसु लघुष्व् अल्पीयसस् तथा ।
4.1.e: Let him prescribe whatever may be befitting for each (case),--heavier (penances) for great (crimes) and easier ones for trivial (faults).

4.1.s: vidhinā śāstradṛṣṭena prāṇāyāmān samācaret | yad upasthakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ padbhyāṃ vā yat kṛtaṃ bhavet | bāhubhyāṃ manasā vācā śrotratvagghrāṇacakṣuṣā |
4.1.d: विधिना शास्त्रदृष्टेन प्राणायामान् समाचरेत् । यद् उपस्थकृतं पापं पद्भ्यां वा यत् कृतं भवेत् । बाहुभ्यां मनसा वाचा श्रोत्रत्वग्घ्राणचक्षुषा ।
4.1.e: Let him perform the penances according to the rule given in the Institutes (of the Sacred Law in cases) where an offence has been committed with the organ or with the feet (and) the arms, through thoughts or speech, through the ear, the skin, the nose or the eye.

4.1.s: api vā cakṣuḥśrotratvagghrāṇamanovyatikrameṣu tribhiḥ prāṇāyāmaiḥ śudhyati |
4.1.d: अपि वा चक्षुःश्रोत्रत्वग्घ्राणमनोव्यतिक्रमेषु त्रिभिः प्राणायामैः शुध्यति ।
4.1.e: Or, in (the case of) transgressions committed through the organ of vision, of hearing, of sensation, of smelling, and through thoughts, he also becomes pure by three suppressions of the breath.

4.1.s: śūdrānnastrīgamanabhojaneṣu kevaleṣu pṛthakpṛthaksaptāhaṃ saptasapta prāṇāyāmān dhārayet |
4.1.d: शूद्रान्नस्त्रीगमनभोजनेषु केवलेषु पृथक्पृथक्सप्ताहं सप्तसप्त प्राणायामान् धारयेत् ।
4.1.e: In case (he commits the offences) of eating the food of a Śūdra or of cohabiting with a Śūdra female, severally, he must perform, during seven days, seven suppressions of the breath on each day.

4.1.s: abhakṣyābhojyāpeyānādyaprāśaneṣu tathāpaṇyavikrayeṣumadhumāṃsaghṛtatailakṣāralavaṇāvarānnavarjeṣu yac cānyad apyevaṃyuktaṃ dvādaśāhaṃ dvādaśadvādaśa prāṇāyāmān dhārayet |
4.1.d: अभक्ष्याभोज्यापेयानाद्यप्राशनेषु तथापण्यविक्रयेषुमधुमांसघृततैलक्षारलवणावरान्नवर्जेषु यच् चान्यद् अप्येवंयुक्तं द्वादशाहं द्वादशद्वादश प्राणायामान् धारयेत् ।
4.1.e: For partaking of food unfit for eating or drinking, and for selling forbidden merchandise, excepting honey, meat, clarified butter, oil, pungent condiments and bad food, and for similar (offences), he must perform, during twelve days, twelve suppressions of the breath on each day.

4.1.s: pātakapatanīyopapātakavarjeṣu yac cānyad apy evaṃyuktamardhamāsaṃ dvādaśadvādaśa prāṇāyāmān dhārayet |
4.1.d: पातकपतनीयोपपातकवर्जेषु यच् चान्यद् अप्य् एवंयुक्तमर्धमासं द्वादशद्वादश प्राणायामान् धारयेत् ।
4.1.e: For other transgressions excepting mortal sins (pātaka), crimes causing loss of caste (patanīya), and the minor faults (called upapātaka), he must perform, during half a month, twelve suppressions of the breath on each day.

4.1.s: pātakapatanīyavarjeṣu yac cānyad apy evaṃyuktaṃ dvādaśadvādaśāhān dvādaśadvādaśa prāṇāyāmān dhārayet |
4.1.d: पातकपतनीयवर्जेषु यच् चान्यद् अप्य् एवंयुक्तं द्वादशद्वादशाहान् द्वादशद्वादश प्राणायामान् धारयेत् ।
4.1.e: For other transgressions excepting mortal sins and crimes causing loss of caste, he must perform, during twelve periods of twelve days, twelve suppressions of the breath on each day.

4.1.s: pātakavarjeṣu yac cānyad apy evaṃyuktaṃ dvādaśārdhamāsāndvādaśadvādaśa prāṇāyāmān dhārayet |
4.1.d: पातकवर्जेषु यच् चान्यद् अप्य् एवंयुक्तं द्वादशार्धमासान्द्वादशद्वादश प्राणायामान् धारयेत् ।
4.1.e: For other transgressions excepting mortal sins he must perform, during twelve half-months, twelve suppressions of the breath on each day.

4.1.s: atha pātakeṣu saṃvatsaraṃ dvādaśadvādaśa prāṇāyāmān dhārayet |
4.1.d: अथ पातकेषु संवत्सरं द्वादशद्वादश प्राणायामान् धारयेत् ।
4.1.e: But for mortal sins he must perform, during a year, twelve suppressions of the breath on each day.

4.1.s: dadyād guṇavate kanyāṃ nagnikāṃ brahmacāriṇe | api vā guṇahīnāya noparundhyād rajasvalām |
4.1.d: दद्याद् गुणवते कन्यां नग्निकां ब्रह्मचारिणे । अपि वा गुणहीनाय नोपरुन्ध्याद् रजस्वलाम् ।
4.1.e: Let him give his daughter, while she still goes naked, to a man who has not broken the vow of chastity and who possesses good qualities, or even to one destitute of good qualities; let him not keep (the maiden) in (his house) after she has reached the age of puberty.

4.1.s: trīṇi varṣāṇy ṛtumatīṃ yaḥ kanyāṃ na prayacchati | sa tulyaṃ bhrūṇahatyāyai doṣam ṛcchaty asaṃśayam |
4.1.d: त्रीणि वर्षाण्य् ऋतुमतीं यः कन्यां न प्रयच्छति । स तुल्यं भ्रूणहत्यायै दोषम् ऋच्छत्य् असंशयम् ।
4.1.e: He who does not give away a marriageable daughter during three years doubtlessly contracts a guilt equal to (that of) destroying an embryo.

4.1.s: na yācate ced evaṃ syād yācate cet pṛthakpṛthak | ekaikasminn ṛtau doṣaṃ pātakaṃ manur abravīt |
4.1.d: न याचते चेद् एवं स्याद् याचते चेत् पृथक्पृथक् । एकैकस्मिन्न् ऋतौ दोषं पातकं मनुर् अब्रवीत् ।
4.1.e: Such will be the case if anybody asks her in marriage, and also if nobody demands her. Manu has declared that at each appearance of the menses (the father incurs the guilt of) a mortal sin.

4.1.s: trīṇi varṣāṇy ṛtumatī kāṅkṣeta pitṛśāsanam | tataś caturthe varṣe tu vindeta sadṛśaṃ patim | avidyamāne sadṛśe guṇahīnam api śrayet |
4.1.d: त्रीणि वर्षाण्य् ऋतुमती काङ्क्षेत पितृशासनम् । ततश् चतुर्थे वर्षे तु विन्देत सदृशं पतिम् । अविद्यमाने सदृशे गुणहीनम् अपि श्रयेत् ।
4.1.e: Three years let a marriageable damsel wait for the order of her father. But after (that) time let her choose for herself in the fourth year a husband (of) equal (rank). If no man (of) equal (rank) be found, she may take even one destitute of good qualities.

4.1.s: balāc cet prahṛtā kanyā mantrair yadi na saṃskṛtā | anyasmai vidhivad deyā yathā kanyā tathaiva sā |
4.1.d: बलाच् चेत् प्रहृता कन्या मन्त्रैर् यदि न संस्कृता । अन्यस्मै विधिवद् देया यथा कन्या तथैव सा ।
4.1.e: If a damsel has been abducted by force, and has not been wedded with sacred texts, she may lawfully be given to another man; she is even like a maiden.

4.1.s: nisṛṣṭāyāṃ hute vāpi yasyai bhartā mriyeta saḥ | sā ced akṣatayoniḥ syād gatapratyāgatā satī | paunarbhavena vidhinā punaḥsaṃskāram arhati |
4.1.d: निसृष्टायां हुते वापि यस्यै भर्ता म्रियेत सः । सा चेद् अक्षतयोनिः स्याद् गतप्रत्यागता सती । पौनर्भवेन विधिना पुनःसंस्कारम् अर्हति ।
4.1.e: If, after (a damsel) has been given away, or even after (the nuptial sacrifices) have been offered, the husband dies, she who (thus) has left (her father's house) and has returned, may be again wedded according to the rule applicable to second weddings, provided the marriage had not been consummated.

4.1.s: trīṇi varṣāṇy ṛtumatīṃ yo bhāryāṃ nādhigacchati | sa tulyaṃ bhrūṇahatyāyai doṣam ṛcchaty asaṃśayam |
4.1.d: त्रीणि वर्षाण्य् ऋतुमतीं यो भार्यां नाधिगच्छति । स तुल्यं भ्रूणहत्यायै दोषम् ऋच्छत्य् असंशयम् ।
4.1.e: He who does not approach, during three years, a wife who is marriageable, incurs, without doubt, a guilt equal to that of destroying an embryo.

4.1.s: ṛtusnātāṃ tu yo bhāryāṃ saṃnidhau nopagacchati | pitaras tasya taṃ māsaṃ tasmin rajasi śerate |
4.1.d: ऋतुस्नातां तु यो भार्यां संनिधौ नोपगच्छति । पितरस् तस्य तं मासं तस्मिन् रजसि शेरते ।
4.1.e: But the ancestors of that man who does not approach his wife who bathed after her temporary uncleanness, though he dwells near her, lie during that month in the menstrual excretions (of the wife).

4.1.s: ṛtau nopaiti yo bhāryām anṛtau yaś ca gacchati | tulyam āhus tayor doṣam ayonau yaś ca siñcati |
4.1.d: ऋतौ नोपैति यो भार्याम् अनृतौ यश् च गच्छति । तुल्यम् आहुस् तयोर् दोषम् अयोनौ यश् च सिञ्चति ।
4.1.e: They declare that the guilt of the husband who does not approach his wife in due season, of him who approaches her during her temporary uncleanness, and of him who commits an unnatural crime (with her), is equally (great).

4.1.s: bhartuḥ pratiniveśena yā bhāryā skandayed ṛtum | tāṃ grāmamadhye vikhyāpya bhrūṇaghnīṃ nirdhamed gṛhāt |
4.1.d: भर्तुः प्रतिनिवेशेन या भार्या स्कन्दयेद् ऋतुम् । तां ग्राममध्ये विख्याप्य भ्रूणघ्नीं निर्धमेद् गृहात् ।
4.1.e: Let him proclaim in the village a wife who, being obdurate against her husband, makes herself sterile, as one who destroys embryos, and drive her from his house.

4.1.s: ṛtusnātāṃ na ced gacchen niyatāṃ dharmacāriṇīm | niyamātikrame tasya prāṇāyāmaśataṃ smṛtam |
4.1.d: ऋतुस्नातां न चेद् गच्छेन् नियतां धर्मचारिणीम् । नियमातिक्रमे तस्य प्राणायामशतं स्मृतम् ।
4.1.e: But for the transgression of that husband who does not approach a wife who bathed after temporary uncleanness, (the performance of) one hundred suppressions of the breath is prescribed (as a penance).

4.1.s: prāṇāyāmān pavitrāṇi vyāhṛtīḥ praṇavaṃ tathā | pavitrapāṇir āsīno brahma naityakam abhyaset |
4.1.d: प्राणायामान् पवित्राणि व्याहृतीः प्रणवं तथा । पवित्रपाणिर् आसीनो ब्रह्म नैत्यकम् अभ्यसेत् ।
4.1.e: Seated with Kuśa grass in his hands, let him repeatedly suppress his breath, and again and again recite purificatory texts, the Vyāh ri tis, the syllable Om, and the daily portion of the Veda.

4.1.s: āvartayet sadā yuktaḥ prāṇāyāmān punaḥpunaḥ | ā keśāntān nakhāgrāc ca tapas tapyata uttamam |
4.1.d: आवर्तयेत् सदा युक्तः प्राणायामान् पुनःपुनः । आ केशान्तान् नखाग्राच् च तपस् तप्यत उत्तमम् ।
4.1.e: Always intent on the practice of Yoga, let him again and again suppress his breath. (Thus) he performs the highest austerity up to the ends of his hair and up to the ends of his nails.

4.1.s: nirodhāj jāyate vāyur vāyor agniś ca jāyate | tāpenāpo 'dhijāyante tato 'ntaḥ śudhyate tribhiḥ |
4.1.d: निरोधाज् जायते वायुर् वायोर् अग्निश् च जायते । तापेनापो ऽधिजायन्ते ततो ऽन्तः शुध्यते त्रिभिः ।
4.1.e: Through the obstruction (of the respiration) air is generated, through air fire is produced, then through heat water is formed; hence he is internally purified by (those) three.

4.1.s: yogenāvāpyate jñānaṃ yogo dharmasya lakṣaṇam | yogamūlā guṇāḥ sarve tasmād yuktaḥ sadā bhavet |
4.1.d: योगेनावाप्यते ज्ञानं योगो धर्मस्य लक्षणम् । योगमूला गुणाः सर्वे तस्माद् युक्तः सदा भवेत् ।
4.1.e: Through the practice of Yoga (true) knowledge is obtained, Yoga is the sum of the sacred law, all good qualities are gained through Yoga; therefore let him always be absorbed in the practice of Yoga.

4.1.s: praṇavādyās trayo vedāḥ praṇave paryavasthitāḥ | praṇavo vyāhṛtayaś caiva nityaṃ brahma sanātanam |
4.1.d: प्रणवाद्यास् त्रयो वेदाः प्रणवे पर्यवस्थिताः । प्रणवो व्याहृतयश् चैव नित्यं ब्रह्म सनातनम् ।
4.1.e: The Vedas likewise begin with the syllable Om, and they end with the syllable Om. The syllable Om and the Vyāh ri tis are the eternal, everlasting Brahman.

4.1.s: praṇave nityayuktasya vyāhṛtīṣu ca saptasu | tripadāyāṃ ca gāyatryāṃ na bhayaṃ vidyate kvacit |
4.1.d: प्रणवे नित्ययुक्तस्य व्याहृतीषु च सप्तसु । त्रिपदायां च गायत्र्यां न भयं विद्यते क्वचित् ।
4.1.e: For him who is constantly engaged in (reciting) the syllable Om, the seven Vyāh ri tis, and the three-footed Gāyatrī, no danger exists anywhere.

4.1.s: savyāhṛtikāṃ sapraṇavāṃ gāyatrīṃ śirasā saha | triḥ paṭhed āyataprāṇaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ sa ucyate |
4.1.d: सव्याहृतिकां सप्रणवां गायत्रीं शिरसा सह । त्रिः पठेद् आयतप्राणः प्राणायामः स उच्यते ।
4.1.e: If, restraining his breath, he thrice recites the Gāyatrī together with the syllable Om and with the (text called) Śiras, that is called one suppression of breath.

4.1.s: savyāhṛtikāḥ sapraṇavāḥ prāṇāyāmās tu ṣoḍaśa | api bhrūṇahanaṃ māsāt punanty aharahardhṛtāḥ |
4.1.d: सव्याहृतिकाः सप्रणवाः प्राणायामास् तु षोडश । अपि भ्रूणहनं मासात् पुनन्त्य् अहरहर्धृताः ।
4.1.e: But sixteen suppressions of breath, accompanied by (the recitation of) the Vyāh ri tis and of the syllable Om, repeated daily, purify after a month even the slayer of a learned Brāhmaṇa.

4.1.s: etadādyaṃ tapaḥ śreṣṭham etad dharmasya lakṣaṇam | sarvadoṣopaghātārtham etad eva viśiṣyate | etad eva viśiṣyata iti |
4.1.d: एतदाद्यं तपः श्रेष्ठम् एतद् धर्मस्य लक्षणम् । सर्वदोषोपघातार्थम् एतद् एव विशिष्यते । एतद् एव विशिष्यत इति ।
4.1.e: That is the highest austerity, that is the best description of the sacred law. That, indeed, is the best means of removing all sin.

4.2.s: prāyaścittāni vakṣyāmo nānārthāni pṛthakpṛthak | teṣuteṣu ca doṣeṣu garīyāṃsi laghūni ca |
4.2.d: प्रायश्चित्तानि वक्ष्यामो नानार्थानि पृथक्पृथक् । तेषुतेषु च दोषेषु गरीयांसि लघूनि च ।
4.2.e: We will separately explain the various penances for the several offences, both heavier and lighter ones.

4.2.s: yady atra hi bhaved yuktaṃ tad hi tatraiva nirdiśet | bhūyobhūyo garīyaḥsu laghuṣv alpīyasas tathā |
4.2.d: यद्य् अत्र हि भवेद् युक्तं तद् हि तत्रैव निर्दिशेत् । भूयोभूयो गरीयःसु लघुष्व् अल्पीयसस् तथा ।
4.2.e: Let him prescribe whatever may be befitting for each (case),--heavier penances for great (crimes), and lighter ones for trivial (faults).
Let him perform the penances according to the rule given in the Institutes of the Sacred Law.

4.2.s: pratigrahīṣyamāṇas tu pratigṛhya tathaiva ca | ṛcas taratsamandyas tu catasraḥ parivartayet |
4.2.d: प्रतिग्रहीष्यमाणस् तु प्रतिगृह्य तथैव च । ऋचस् तरत्समन्द्यस् तु चतस्रः परिवर्तयेत् ।
4.2.e: He who is about to accept gifts, or he who has accepted gifts, must repeatedly recite the four Ri k-verses (called) Taratsamandīs.

4.2.s: abhojyānāṃ tu sarveṣām abhojyānnasya bhojane | ṛgbhis taratsamandībhir mārjanaṃpāpaśodhanam |
4.2.d: अभोज्यानां तु सर्वेषाम् अभोज्यान्नस्य भोजने । ऋग्भिस् तरत्समन्दीभिर् मार्जनंपापशोधनम् ।
4.2.e: But in case one has eaten any kind of forbidden food; or that given by a person whose food must not be eaten, the means of removing the guilt is to sprinkle water (over one's head) while one recites the Taratsamandī Ri k as.

4.2.s: bhrūṇahatyāvidhis tv anyas taṃ tu vakṣyāmy ataḥ param | vidhinā yena mucyante pātakebhyo 'pi sarvaśaḥ |
4.2.d: भ्रूणहत्याविधिस् त्व् अन्यस् तं तु वक्ष्याम्य् अतः परम् । विधिना येन मुच्यन्ते पातकेभ्यो ऽपि सर्वशः ।
4.2.e: But we will, hereafter, declare another rule for (the expiation of) the murder of a learned Brāhmaṇa, whereby (men) are freed also from mortal sins of all (kinds).

4.2.s: prāṇāyāmān pavitrāṇi vyāhṛtīḥ praṇavaṃ tathā | japed aghamarṣaṇaṃ sūktaṃ payasā dvādaśa kṣapāḥ |
4.2.d: प्राणायामान् पवित्राणि व्याहृतीः प्रणवं तथा । जपेद् अघमर्षणं सूक्तं पयसा द्वादश क्षपाः ।
4.2.e: Let him (perform), during twelve nights, suppressions of the breath (and) mutter purificatory texts, the Vyāh ri tis, the syllable Om, (and) the Aghamarshaṇa hymn, (living) on milk;

4.2.s: trirātraṃ vāyubhakṣo vā klinnavāsāḥ plutaḥ śuciḥ |
4.2.d: त्रिरात्रं वायुभक्षो वा क्लिन्नवासाः प्लुतः शुचिः ।
4.2.e: Or (he becomes) pure if he bathes, and during three (days and) nights subsists on air and (remains dressed) in wet clothes.

4.2.s: pratiṣiddhāṃs tathācārān abhyasyāpi punaḥpunaḥ | vāruṇībhir upasthāya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate || iti |
4.2.d: प्रतिषिद्धांस् तथाचारान् अभ्यस्यापि पुनःपुनः । वारुणीभिर् उपस्थाय सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥ इति ।
4.2.e: But if he has repeatedly committed forbidden acts of all kinds, and has (afterwards) worshipped reciting the Vāruṇī (texts), he is freed from all sin.

4.2.s: athāvakīrṇy amāvāsyāyāṃ niśy agnim upasamādhāyadārvihomikīṃ pariceṣṭāṃ kṛtvā dve ājyāhutī juhoti | kāmaavakīrṇo 'smy avakīrṇo 'smi kāma kāmāya svāhā | kāmaabhidrugdho 'smy abhidrugdho 'smi kāma kāmāya svāheti |
4.2.d: अथावकीर्ण्य् अमावास्यायां निश्य् अग्निम् उपसमाधायदार्विहोमिकीं परिचेष्टां कृत्वा द्वे आज्याहुती जुहोति । कामअवकीर्णो ऽस्म्य् अवकीर्णो ऽस्मि काम कामाय स्वाहा । कामअभिद्रुग्धो ऽस्म्य् अभिद्रुग्धो ऽस्मि काम कामाय स्वाहेति ।
4.2.e: Now a student who has broken his vow (avakīrṇin) shall heap fuel on the fire on the night of the new moon, perform the preparatory ceremonies required for a Darvīhoma, and offer two oblations of clarified butter (reciting the following texts): 'O Lust, I have broken my vow, my vow I have broken, O Lust, to. Lust Svāhā;' 'O Lust, I have done evil, I have done evil, O Lust, to Lust Svāhā.'

4.2.s: hutvā prayatāñjaliḥ kavātiryaṅṅ agnim upatiṣṭheta | saṃ mā siñcantu marutaḥ sam indraḥ saṃ bṛhaspatiḥ | saṃ māyam agniḥ siñcatvāyuṣā ca balena cāyuṣmantaṃ karota meti | prati hāsmai marutaḥ prāṇān dadhati prati indro balaṃ pratibṛhaspatir brahmavarcasaṃ praty agnir itarat sarvam | sarvatanur bhūtvāsarvam āyur eti | trir abhimantrayeta | triṣatyā hi devā iti vijñāyate |
4.2.d: हुत्वा प्रयताञ्जलिः कवातिर्यङ्ङ् अग्निम् उपतिष्ठेत । सं मा सिञ्चन्तु मरुतः सम् इन्द्रः सं बृहस्पतिः । सं मायम् अग्निः सिञ्चत्वायुषा च बलेन चायुष्मन्तं करोत मेति । प्रति हास्मै मरुतः प्राणान् दधति प्रति इन्द्रो बलं प्रतिबृहस्पतिर् ब्रह्मवर्चसं प्रत्य् अग्निर् इतरत् सर्वम् । सर्वतनुर् भूत्वासर्वम् आयुर् एति । त्रिर् अभिमन्त्रयेत । त्रिषत्या हि देवा इति विज्ञायते ।
4.2.e: After he has made the offering, he shall address the fire, closely joining his hands and turning sideways, (with the following texts): 'May the Maruts grant me, may Indra, may B ri haspati,, may this fire grant me long life and strength, make me long-lived.' The Maruts, forsooth, give back to him the vital airs, Indra gives back to him strength, B ri haspati the lustre of Brahman, Fire all the remainder. (Thus) his body is made whole, and he attains the full length of life. Let him next address (the gods) with three (repetitions of the texts). [paragraph continues] For the gods are trebly true. (All that) has been declared in the Veda.

4.2.s: yo 'pūta iva manyeta ātmānam upapātakaiḥ | sa hutvaitena vidhinā sarvasmāt pāpāt pramucyate |
4.2.d: यो ऽपूत इव मन्येत आत्मानम् उपपातकैः । स हुत्वैतेन विधिना सर्वस्मात् पापात् प्रमुच्यते ।
4.2.e: He who considers himself defiled by minor offences (upapātaka), will be freed from all guilt if he offers burnt oblations according to this same rule;

4.2.s: api vānādyāpeyapratiṣiddhabhojaneṣu doṣavac ca karma kṛtvābhisaṃdhipūrvam anabhisaṃdhipūrvaṃ vā śūdrāyāṃ ca retaḥ siktvāyonau vābliṅgābhir vāruṇībhiś copaspṛśya prayato bhavati |
4.2.d: अपि वानाद्यापेयप्रतिषिद्धभोजनेषु दोषवच् च कर्म कृत्वाभिसंधिपूर्वम् अनभिसंधिपूर्वं वा शूद्रायां च रेतः सिक्त्वायोनौ वाब्लिङ्गाभिर् वारुणीभिश् चोपस्पृश्य प्रयतो भवति ।
4.2.e: Or if he has partaken of food unfit to be eaten or to be drunk or of forbidden food, and if he has committed sinful acts or performed sinful rites either unintentionally or intentionally, and if he has had connexion with a female of the Śūdra caste or committed an unnatural crime, he becomes pure by bathing (and reciting) the Abliṅga (verses) and (those called) Vāruṇīs.

4.2.s: athāpy udāharanti | anādyāpeyapratiṣiddhabhojane viruddhadharmācarite ca karmaṇi | matipravṛtte 'pi ca pātakopamair viśudhyate 'thāpi casarvapātakaiḥ |
4.2.d: अथाप्य् उदाहरन्ति । अनाद्यापेयप्रतिषिद्धभोजने विरुद्धधर्माचरिते च कर्मणि । मतिप्रवृत्ते ऽपि च पातकोपमैर् विशुध्यते ऽथापि चसर्वपातकैः ।
4.2.e: Now they quote also (the following verse): If he has partaken of food unfit to be eaten or to be drunk, or of forbidden food, and if he has committed forbidden acts or performed forbidden rites, he will, nevertheless, be freed from (crimes) committed intentionally which are similar to mortal sins, nay, even from mortal sins (pātaka).'

4.2.s: trirātraṃ vāpy upavasaṃs trir ahno 'bhyupayann apaḥ | prāṇān ātmani saṃyamya triḥ paṭhed aghamarṣaṇam | yathāśvamedhāvabhṛtha evaṃ tan manur abravīt |
4.2.d: त्रिरात्रं वाप्य् उपवसंस् त्रिर् अह्नो ऽभ्युपयन्न् अपः । प्राणान् आत्मनि संयम्य त्रिः पठेद् अघमर्षणम् । यथाश्वमेधावभृथ एवं तन् मनुर् अब्रवीत् ।
4.2.e: Or let him fast during three (days and) nights, bathe thrice a day, and, suppressing his breath, thrice recite the Aghamarshaṇa. Manu has declared that that is equal (in efficacy) to the final bath at a horse-sacrifice.

4.2.s: vijñāyate ca | caraṇaṃ pavitraṃ vitataṃ purāṇaṃ yena pūtas tarati duṣkṛtāni | tena pavitreṇa śuddhena pūtā ati pāpmānam arātiṃ tarema || iti |
4.2.d: विज्ञायते च । चरणं पवित्रं विततं पुराणं येन पूतस् तरति दुष्कृतानि । तेन पवित्रेण शुद्धेन पूता अति पाप्मानम् अरातिं तरेम ॥ इति ।
4.2.e: And it is declared in the Veda, '(That is) the ancient purificatory rite, which is widely known (in the Institutes of the Sacred Law); purified thereby man conquers sin. May we, sanctified by this holy means of purification, conquer our enemy, sin.'

4.3.s: prāyaścittāni vakṣyāmo 'vikhyātāni viśeṣataḥ | samāhitānāṃ yuktānāṃ pramādeṣu kathaṃ bhavet |
4.3.d: प्रायश्चित्तानि वक्ष्यामो ऽविख्यातानि विशेषतः । समाहितानां युक्तानां प्रमादेषु कथं भवेत् ।
4.3.e: We will explain the (secret) penances which are not prescribed (by others, but by the offender himself, and) particularly what shall be done in (case) faults (have been committed) by men who, with concentrated minds, (are) intent (on the performance of their duties).
(Such a man) may sip water, (in order to atone) for all mortal sins, reciting the syllable Om and all the Vyāh ri tis.

4.3.s: yat prathamam ācāmati tenargvedaṃ prīṇāti yad dvitīyaṃ tenayajurvedaṃ yat tṛtīyaṃ tena sāmavedam |
4.3.d: यत् प्रथमम् आचामति तेनर्ग्वेदं प्रीणाति यद् द्वितीयं तेनयजुर्वेदं यत् तृतीयं तेन सामवेदम् ।
4.3.e: When he sips water the first time, he gladdens the Rig-veda, the second time the Ya g ur-veda, the third time the Sāma-veda.

4.3.s: yat prathamaṃ parimārṣṭi tenātharvavedaṃ yad dvitīyaṃtenetihāsapurāṇam |
4.3.d: यत् प्रथमं परिमार्ष्टि तेनाथर्ववेदं यद् द्वितीयंतेनेतिहासपुराणम् ।
4.3.e: When he wipes (his lips) the first time, he gladdens the Atharva-veda, the second time the Itihāsas and Purāṇas.

4.3.s: yat savyaṃ pāṇiṃ prokṣati pādau śiro hṛdayaṃ nāsike cakṣuṣīśrotre nābhiṃ copaspṛśati tenauṣadhivanaspatayaḥ sarvāś ca devatāḥ prīṇāti | tasmād ācamanād eva sarvasmāt pāpāt pramucyate |
4.3.d: यत् सव्यं पाणिं प्रोक्षति पादौ शिरो हृदयं नासिके चक्षुषीश्रोत्रे नाभिं चोपस्पृशति तेनौषधिवनस्पतयः सर्वाश् च देवताः प्रीणाति । तस्माद् आचमनाद् एव सर्वस्मात् पापात् प्रमुच्यते ।
4.3.e: When he sprinkles water on the right hand, the feet, the head, the heart, the nostrils, the eyes, the ears, and the navel, he gladdens the trees and herbs and all deities. Therefore he is freed from all sin by sipping water.

4.3.s: aṣṭau vā samidha ādadhyāt | devakṛtasyainaso 'vayajanam asisvāhā | manuṣyakṛtasyainaso 'vayajanam asi svāhā | pitṛkṛtasyainaso 'vayajanam asi svāhā | ātmakṛtasyainaso 'vayajanam asi svāhā | yad divā ca naktaṃ cainaś cakṛma tasyāvayajanam asisvāhā | yat svapantaś ca jāgrataś cainaś cakṛma tasyāvayajanam asisvāhā | yad vidvāṃsaś cāvidvāṃsaś cainaś cakṛma tasyāvayajanam asi svāhā | enasa enaso 'vayajanam asi svāheti |
4.3.d: अष्टौ वा समिध आदध्यात् । देवकृतस्यैनसो ऽवयजनम् असिस्वाहा । मनुष्यकृतस्यैनसो ऽवयजनम् असि स्वाहा । पितृकृतस्यैनसो ऽवयजनम् असि स्वाहा । आत्मकृतस्यैनसो ऽवयजनम् असि स्वाहा । यद् दिवा च नक्तं चैनश् चकृम तस्यावयजनम् असिस्वाहा । यत् स्वपन्तश् च जाग्रतश् चैनश् चकृम तस्यावयजनम् असिस्वाहा । यद् विद्वांसश् चाविद्वांसश् चैनश् चकृम तस्यावयजनम् असि स्वाहा । एनस एनसो ऽवयजनम् असि स्वाहेति ।
4.3.e: Or let him offer in the fire eight pieces of sacred fuel, reciting (the following) eight (texts): 'Thou art the expiation of sin committed by the gods, Svāhā;' 'Thou art the expiation of sin committed by men, Svāhā;' 'Thou art the expiation of sin committed by the manes, Svāhā;' 'Thou art the expiation of sin committed by myself, Svāhā;' 'Thou art the expiation of the sift which we have committed either by day or by night, Svāhā;" Thou art the expiation of the sin which we have committed either sleeping or waking, Svāhā;' 'Thou art the expiation of the sin which we have committed either intentionally or unintentionally, Svāhā;' Thou art the expiation of every sin, Svāhā.'

4.3.s: etair aṣṭābhir hutvā sarvasmāt pāpāt pramucyate |
4.3.d: एतैर् अष्टाभिर् हुत्वा सर्वस्मात् पापात् प्रमुच्यते ।
4.3.e: When he has offered (these eight oblations) he will be freed from all guilt.

4.3.s: athāpy udāharanti | aghamarṣaṇaṃ devakṛtaṃ śuddhavatyas taratsamāḥ | kūśmāṇḍyaḥ pāvamānyaś ca virajā mṛtyulāṅgalam | durgā vyāhṛtayo rudrā mahādoṣavināśanāḥ | mahādoṣavināśanā iti |
4.3.d: अथाप्य् उदाहरन्ति । अघमर्षणं देवकृतं शुद्धवत्यस् तरत्समाः । कूश्माण्ड्यः पावमान्यश् च विरजा मृत्युलाङ्गलम् । दुर्गा व्याहृतयो रुद्रा महादोषविनाशनाः । महादोषविनाशना इति ।
4.3.e: Now they quote also (the following verse): 'The Aghamarshaṇa, the Devak ri ta, the Suddhavatīs, the Taratsamās, the Kūshmāṇd īs, the Pāvamānīs, the Virā g ās, the M ri tyulāṅgala, the Durgā (Sāvitrī), the Vyāh ri tis, and the Rudras (are texts) which are very efficacious for effacing sin.'

4.4.s: prāyaścittāni vakṣyāmo 'vikhyātāni viśeṣataḥ | samāhitānāṃ yuktānāṃ pramādeṣu kathaṃ bhavet |
4.4.d: प्रायश्चित्तानि वक्ष्यामो ऽविख्यातानि विशेषतः । समाहितानां युक्तानां प्रमादेषु कथं भवेत् ।
4.4.e: We will explain the (secret) penances which are not prescribed (by others, but by the offender himself, and) particularly what shall be done in (case) faults (have been committed) by men who, with concentrated minds, (are) intent (on the performance of their duties).

4.4.s: ṛtaṃ ca satyaṃ ceti | etad aghamarṣaṇaṃ trir antarjale paṭhansarvasmāt pāpāt pramucyate |
4.4.d: ऋतं च सत्यं चेति । एतद् अघमर्षणं त्रिर् अन्तर्जले पठन्सर्वस्मात् पापात् प्रमुच्यते ।
4.4.e: He who, standing in water, thrice recites that (hymn of) Aghamarshaṇa (which begins), 'Both right and truth,' will be freed from all guilt.

4.4.s: āyaṃ gauḥ pṛśnir akramīd iti | etām ṛcaṃ trir antarjale paṭhansarvasmāt pāpāt pramucyate |
4.4.d: आयं गौः पृश्निर् अक्रमीद् इति । एताम् ऋचं त्रिर् अन्तर्जले पठन्सर्वस्मात् पापात् प्रमुच्यते ।
4.4.e: He who, standing in water, thrice recites the verse, 'This spotted bull,' &c., will be freed from all guilt;

4.4.s: drupadād iven mumucāna iti | etām ṛcaṃ trir antarjalepaṭhan sarvasmāt pāpāt pramucyate |
4.4.d: द्रुपदाद् इवेन् मुमुचान इति । एताम् ऋचं त्रिर् अन्तर्जलेपठन् सर्वस्मात् पापात् प्रमुच्यते ।
4.4.e: He who, standing in water, thrice recites the verse, 'Freed from the post as it were,' will be freed from all guilt.

4.4.s: haṃsaḥ śuciṣad iti | etām ṛcaṃ trir antarjale paṭhan sarvasmātpāpāt pramucyate |
4.4.d: हंसः शुचिषद् इति । एताम् ऋचं त्रिर् अन्तर्जले पठन् सर्वस्मात्पापात् प्रमुच्यते ।
4.4.e: He who, standing in water, thrice recites the verse, 'A swan dwelling in purity,' will be freed from all guilt;

4.4.s: api vā sāvitrīṃ paccho 'rdharcaśastataḥ samastāṃ trir antarjale paṭhan sarvasmātpāpāt pramucyate |
4.4.d: अपि वा सावित्रीं पच्छो ऽर्धर्चशस्ततः समस्तां त्रिर् अन्तर्जले पठन् सर्वस्मात्पापात् प्रमुच्यते ।
4.4.e: Or, he who, standing in water, thrice recites the Sāvitrī, foot by foot, half verse by half verse, and afterwards entire, will be freed from all guilt;

4.4.s: api vā vyāhṛtīr vyastāḥ samastāś ceti trir antarjale paṭhansarvasmāt pāpāt pramucyate |
4.4.d: अपि वा व्याहृतीर् व्यस्ताः समस्ताश् चेति त्रिर् अन्तर्जले पठन्सर्वस्मात् पापात् प्रमुच्यते ।
4.4.e: Or, he who, standing in water, thrice recites the Vyāh ri tis, both separately and altogether, will be freed from all guilt;

4.4.s: api vā praṇavam eva trir antarjale paṭhan sarvasmāt pāpāt pramucyate |
4.4.d: अपि वा प्रणवम् एव त्रिर् अन्तर्जले पठन् सर्वस्मात् पापात् प्रमुच्यते ।
4.4.e: Or, he who, standing in water, thrice recites the syllable Om alone, will be freed from all guilt.

4.4.s: tad etad dharmaśāstraṃ nāputrāya nāśiṣyāya nāsaṃvatsaroṣitāya dadyāt |
4.4.d: तद् एतद् धर्मशास्त्रं नापुत्राय नाशिष्याय नासंवत्सरोषिताय दद्यात् ।
4.4.e: Let him not teach these Institutes of the Sacred Law to one who is neither his son nor his pupil, nor has resided (in his house) less than a year.

4.4.s: sahasraṃ dakṣiṇa ṛṣabhaikādaśaṃ guruprasādo vā | guruprasādo vā |
4.4.d: सहस्रं दक्षिण ऋषभैकादशं गुरुप्रसादो वा । गुरुप्रसादो वा ।
4.4.e: The fee (for teaching it) is one thousand (paṇas, or) ten cows and a bull, or the worship of the teacher.

4.5.s: athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi sāmargyajuratharvaṇām | karmabhir yair avāpnoti kṣipraṃ kāmān manogatān |
4.5.d: अथातः संप्रवक्ष्यामि सामर्ग्यजुरथर्वणाम् । कर्मभिर् यैर् अवाप्नोति क्षिप्रं कामान् मनोगतान् ।
4.5.e: Now, therefore, I will proclaim by what rites, connected with the Sāman, Rik, Ya g us, and Atharva-vedas, [paragraph continues] (man) quickly attains the wishes of his heart.

4.5.s: japahomeṣṭiyantrādyaiḥ śodhayitvā svavigraham | sādhayet sarvakarmāṇi nānyathā siddhim aśnute |
4.5.d: जपहोमेष्टियन्त्राद्यैः शोधयित्वा स्वविग्रहम् । साधयेत् सर्वकर्माणि नान्यथा सिद्धिम् अश्नुते ।
4.5.e: Having purified his body by muttered prayers, burnt oblations, Ishṭis, restraints, and the like, he will accomplish all his objects. He will not attain success in any other way.

4.5.s: japahomeṣṭiyantrāṇi kariṣyann ādito dvijaḥ | śuklapuṇyadinarkṣeṣu keśaśmaśrūṇi vāpayet |
4.5.d: जपहोमेष्टियन्त्राणि करिष्यन्न् आदितो द्विजः । शुक्लपुण्यदिनर्क्षेषु केशश्मश्रूणि वापयेत् ।
4.5.e: A Brāhmaṇa, who is going to mutter prayers, to offer burnt oblations or Ishṭis, or to practise restraints, shall, first, during the bright half of the month, on a lucky day and under a lucky constellation, cause his hair and beard to be cut.

4.5.s: snāyāt triṣavaṇaṃ pāyād ātmānaṃkrodhato 'nṛtāt | strīśūdrair nābhibhāṣeta brahmacārī havirvrataḥ |
4.5.d: स्नायात् त्रिषवणं पायाद् आत्मानंक्रोधतो ऽनृतात् । स्त्रीशूद्रैर् नाभिभाषेत ब्रह्मचारी हविर्व्रतः ।
4.5.e: Let him bathe in the morning, at noon, and in the evening; let him beware of anger and untruth; let him not address women and Śūdras; let him be continent, and subsist solely on food fit for offerings.

4.5.s: goviprapitṛdevebhyo namaskuryād divāsvapan | japahomeṣṭiyantrastho divāsthāno niśāsanaḥ |
4.5.d: गोविप्रपितृदेवेभ्यो नमस्कुर्याद् दिवास्वपन् । जपहोमेष्टियन्त्रस्थो दिवास्थानो निशासनः ।
4.5.e: Avoiding to sleep in the day-time, let him worship cows, Brāhmaṇas, manes, and gods. As long as he is engaged in muttering prayers, offering Homas and Ishṭis, and practising restraints, let him stand during the day and sit during the night.

4.5.s: prājāpatyo bhavet kṛcchro divā rātrāv ayācitam | kramaśo vāyubhakṣaś ca dvādaśāhaṃ tryahaṃtryaham |
4.5.d: प्राजापत्यो भवेत् कृच्छ्रो दिवा रात्राव् अयाचितम् । क्रमशो वायुभक्षश् च द्वादशाहं त्र्यहंत्र्यहम् ।
4.5.e: The K ri k kh ra (penance) revealed by Pra g āpati lasts twelve days, (which are divided into four separate) periods of three days; (during the first period of three days he eats) in the day-time (only, during the second) at night (only, during the third he subsists on) food given without asking, (and during the fourth) finally (he lives on) air.

4.5.s: ahar ekaṃ tathā naktam ajñātaṃ vāyubhakṣaṇam | trivṛd eṣa parāvṛtto bālānāṃ kṛcchra ucyate |
4.5.d: अहर् एकं तथा नक्तम् अज्ञातं वायुभक्षणम् । त्रिवृद् एष परावृत्तो बालानां कृच्छ्र उच्यते ।
4.5.e: (If one eats on) one (day in) the morning (only), and (on the following day) at night (only, on the next day food) given without asking, (and on the fourth day) subsists on air, and repeats this three times, that is called the K ri k kh ra (penance) of children.

4.5.s: ekaikaṃ grāsam aśnīyāt pūrvoktena tryahaṃtryaham | vāyubhakṣas tryahaṃ cānyad atikṛcchraḥ sa ucyate |
4.5.d: एकैकं ग्रासम् अश्नीयात् पूर्वोक्तेन त्र्यहंत्र्यहम् । वायुभक्षस् त्र्यहं चान्यद् अतिकृच्छ्रः स उच्यते ।
4.5.e: (If) one eats one mouthful only at each (meal), following, during (three) periods of three days, the rules given above, and subsists during another period of three days on air, that is called the Atik ri k kh ra penance.

4.5.s: ambubhakṣas tryahān etān vāyubhakṣas tataḥ param | kṛcchrātikṛcchras tṛtīyo vijñeyaḥ so 'tipāvanaḥ |
4.5.d: अम्बुभक्षस् त्र्यहान् एतान् वायुभक्षस् ततः परम् । कृच्छ्रातिकृच्छ्रस् तृतीयो विज्ञेयः सो ऽतिपावनः ।
4.5.e: (If) during those (first) three periods of three days one partakes of water only, and subsists afterwards (during three days) on air, that third (variety) must be known to be the most efficacious K ri k kh rātik ri k kh ra penance.

4.5.s: tryahaṃtryahaṃ pibed uṣṇaṃ payaḥ sarpiḥ kuśodakam | vāyubhakṣas tryahaṃ cānyat taptakṛcchraḥ sa ucyate |
4.5.d: त्र्यहंत्र्यहं पिबेद् उष्णं पयः सर्पिः कुशोदकम् । वायुभक्षस् त्र्यहं चान्यत् तप्तकृच्छ्रः स उच्यते ।
4.5.e: If one drinks hot milk, (hot) clarified butter, (and a hot) decoction of Kuśa grass, each during three days, and fasts during another three days, that is called the Taptak ri k kh ra.

4.5.s: gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam | ekarātropavāsaś ca kṛcchraḥ sāṃtapanaḥ smṛtaḥ |
4.5.d: गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिः कुशोदकम् । एकरात्रोपवासश् च कृच्छ्रः सांतपनः स्मृतः ।
4.5.e: (If one lives during one day) on cow's urine, (during one day) on cowdung, (during one day) on milk, (during one day) on sour milk, (during one day) on clarified butter, (during one day) on a decoction of Kuśa grass, and during one (day and) night on air, that is called the Sāṃtāpana K ri k kh ra.

4.5.s: gāyatryādāya gomūtraṃgandhadvāreti gomayam | ā pyāyasveti ca kṣīraṃ dadhikrāvṇeti vai dadhi | śukram asi jyotir ity ājyaṃ devasyatveti kuśodakam |
4.5.d: गायत्र्यादाय गोमूत्रंगन्धद्वारेति गोमयम् । आ प्यायस्वेति च क्षीरं दधिक्राव्णेति वै दधि । शुक्रम् असि ज्योतिर् इत्य् आज्यं देवस्यत्वेति कुशोदकम् ।
4.5.e: Let him take the cow's urine, reciting the Gāyatrī; the cowdung, (reciting the text), 'Gandhadvārām;' the milk, (reciting the verse), 'Āpyāyasva;' the sour milk, reciting (the verse), 'Dadhikrāvṇā;' the clarified butter, (saying), ' Śukram asi;' the decoction of Kuśa grass (with the text), 'Devasya tvā;'

4.5.s: gomūtrabhāgas tasyārdhaṃ śakṛt kṣīrasya tu trayam | dvayaṃ dadhno ghṛtasyaika ekaś ca kuśavāriṇaḥ | evaṃ sāṃtapanaḥ kṛcchraḥ śvapākam api śodhayet |
4.5.d: गोमूत्रभागस् तस्यार्धं शकृत् क्षीरस्य तु त्रयम् । द्वयं दध्नो घृतस्यैक एकश् च कुशवारिणः । एवं सांतपनः कृच्छ्रः श्वपाकम् अपि शोधयेत् ।
4.5.e: (And mix together) one part of cow's urine, half as much .cowdung, three parts of milk, two of sour milk, one part of clarified butter, and one part of water boiled with Kuśa grass;' a Sāṃtāpana K ri k kh ra (performed) in this manner will purify even a Śvapāka.

4.5.s: gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ caiva kṣīraṃ dadhi ghṛtaṃ tathā | pañcarātraṃ tadāhāraḥ pañcagavyena śudhyati |
4.5.d: गोमूत्रं गोमयं चैव क्षीरं दधि घृतं तथा । पञ्चरात्रं तदाहारः पञ्चगव्येन शुध्यति ।
4.5.e: He who subsists during five (days and) nights on cow's urine, cowdung, milk, sour milk, and clarified butter will be purified by (that) Pa ñ k agavya (the five products of the cow).

4.5.s: yat ātmano 'pramattasya dvādaśāham abhojanam | parāko nāma kṛcchro 'yaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanaḥ |
4.5.d: यत् आत्मनो ऽप्रमत्तस्य द्वादशाहम् अभोजनम् । पराको नाम कृच्छ्रो ऽयं सर्वपापप्रणाशनः ।
4.5.e: If, self-restrained and attentive, he fasts during twelve days, that is called a Parāka K ri k kh ra, which destroys all sin.

4.5.s: gomūtrādibhir abhyastam ekaikaṃ taṃ trisaptakam | mahāsāṃtapanaṃ kṛcchraṃ vadanti brahmavādinaḥ |
4.5.d: गोमूत्रादिभिर् अभ्यस्तम् एकैकं तं त्रिसप्तकम् । महासांतपनं कृच्छ्रं वदन्ति ब्रह्मवादिनः ।
4.5.e: If he subsists on cow's urine and the other (substances named above), one day on each, and continues (this mode of life) during thrice seven days, the theologians call that a Mahāsāṃtāpana K ri k kh ra.

4.5.s: ekavṛddhyā site piṇḍān ekahānyāsite tataḥ | pakṣayor upavāsau dvau tad hi cāndrāyaṇaṃ smṛtam |
4.5.d: एकवृद्ध्या सिते पिण्डान् एकहान्यासिते ततः । पक्षयोर् उपवासौ द्वौ तद् हि चान्द्रायणं स्मृतम् ।
4.5.e: If he daily adds to his food one mouthful during the bright (half of the month) and diminishes it daily by one mouthful during the dark (half of the month), and keeps two fasts in the two halves of the month, that is called a K āndrāyaṇa.

4.5.s: caturaḥ prātar aśnīyāt piṇḍān vipraḥ samāhitaḥ | caturo 'stamite sūrye śiśucāndrāyaṇaṃ caret |
4.5.d: चतुरः प्रातर् अश्नीयात् पिण्डान् विप्रः समाहितः । चतुरो ऽस्तमिते सूर्ये शिशुचान्द्रायणं चरेत् ।
4.5.e: If, with concentrated mind, a Brāhmaṇa eats four mouthfuls in the morning and four mouthfuls when the sun has set, he will perform the K āndrāyaṇa of children.

4.5.s: aṣṭāvaṣṭau māsam ekaṃ piṇḍān madhyaṃdine sthite | niyatātmā haviṣyasya yaticāndrāyaṇaṃ caret |
4.5.d: अष्टावष्टौ मासम् एकं पिण्डान् मध्यंदिने स्थिते । नियतात्मा हविष्यस्य यतिचान्द्रायणं चरेत् ।
4.5.e: If, self-restrained, he daily eats, during a month, at midday eight mouthfuls of food, fit for a sacrifice, he will perform the K āndrāyaṇa of ascetics.

4.5.s: yathā kathaṃcit piṇḍānāṃ dvijas tisras tv aśītayaḥ | māsenāśnan haviṣyasya candrasyaiti salokatām |
4.5.d: यथा कथंचित् पिण्डानां द्विजस् तिस्रस् त्व् अशीतयः । मासेनाश्नन् हविष्यस्य चन्द्रस्यैति सलोकताम् ।
4.5.e: But a Brāhmaṇa who eats anyhow, during a month, thrice eighty mouthfuls of food, fit for a sacrifice, goes to the world of the moon.

4.5.s: yathodyaṃś candramā hanti jagatas tamaso bhayam | evaṃ pāpād bhayaṃ hanti dvijaś cāndrāyaṇaṃ caran |
4.5.d: यथोद्यंश् चन्द्रमा हन्ति जगतस् तमसो भयम् । एवं पापाद् भयं हन्ति द्विजश् चान्द्रायणं चरन् ।
4.5.e: As the rising moon frees the world from the fear of darkness, even so a Brāhmaṇa who performs a K āndrāyaṇa removes the fear of sin.

4.5.s: kaṇapiṇyākatakrāṇi yavācāmo 'nilāśanaḥ | ekatripañcasapteti pāpaghno 'yaṃ tulāpumān |
4.5.d: कणपिण्याकतक्राणि यवाचामो ऽनिलाशनः । एकत्रिपञ्चसप्तेति पापघ्नो ऽयं तुलापुमान् ।
4.5.e: He who lives one day on (rice)-grains, three days on oil-cakes, 'five days on buttermilk mixed with water, seven days on water, and (one day) on air, (performs) the guilt-destroying Tulāpurusha.

4.5.s: yāvakaḥ saptarātreṇa vṛjinaṃ hanti dehinām | saptarātropavāso vā dṛṣṭam etan manīṣibhiḥ |
4.5.d: यावकः सप्तरात्रेण वृजिनं हन्ति देहिनाम् । सप्तरात्रोपवासो वा दृष्टम् एतन् मनीषिभिः ।
4.5.e: Living on barley-gruel (yāvaka) removes the guilt of corporeal beings after seven days, and so does a fast of seven days; that has been recognised by wise men.

4.5.s: pauṣabhādrapadajyeṣṭhāsv ārdrākāśātapāśrayāt | trīñ śuklān mucyate pāpāt patanīyād ṛte dvijaḥ |
4.5.d: पौषभाद्रपदज्येष्ठास्व् आर्द्राकाशातपाश्रयात् । त्रीञ् शुक्लान् मुच्यते पापात् पतनीयाद् ऋते द्विजः ।
4.5.e: By dressing in wet clothes, by living in the open air, and by exposing himself to the sun during the light halves of the months Pausha (December-January), Bhādrapada (August-September), and Gyesh th a (May-June), a Brāhmaṇa is freed from (all) sin excepting crimes causing loss of caste (patanīya).

4.5.s: gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam | yavācāmena saṃyukto brahmakūrco 'tipāvanaḥ |
4.5.d: गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिः कुशोदकम् । यवाचामेन संयुक्तो ब्रह्मकूर्चो ऽतिपावनः ।
4.5.e: (If one swallows) cows' urine, cowdung, milk, sour milk, clarified butter, and a decoction of Kuśa grass, mixed with barley gruel, that is the most sanctifying Brahmakūr k a.

4.5.s: amāvāsyāṃ nirāhāraḥ paurṇamāsyāṃ tilāśanaḥ | śuklakṛṣṇakṛtāt pāpān mucyate abdasya parvabhiḥ |
4.5.d: अमावास्यां निराहारः पौर्णमास्यां तिलाशनः । शुक्लकृष्णकृतात् पापान् मुच्यते अब्दस्य पर्वभिः ।
4.5.e: He who fasts on the new moon day and eats sesamum grains on the full moon day, will be freed in the course of a year from the sins which he committed in the bright and the dark halves of the month.

4.5.s: bhaikṣāhāro 'gnihotribhyo māsenaikena śudhyati | yāyāvaravanasthebhyo daśabhiḥ pañcabhir dinaiḥ |
4.5.d: भैक्षाहारो ऽग्निहोत्रिभ्यो मासेनैकेन शुध्यति । यायावरवनस्थेभ्यो दशभिः पञ्चभिर् दिनैः ।
4.5.e: He who lives on alms obtained from Agnihotrins is purified in one month; (he who obtains his food) from a Yāyāvara. in ten days; he who receives it from a hermit in the forest, in five days;

4.5.s: ekāhadhanino 'nnena dinenaikena śudhyati | kāpotavṛttiniṣṭhasya pītvāpaḥ śudhyate tribhiḥ |
4.5.d: एकाहधनिनो ऽन्नेन दिनेनैकेन शुध्यति । कापोतवृत्तिनिष्ठस्य पीत्वापः शुध्यते त्रिभिः ।
4.5.e: (He who lives) on food given by a person who has a store sufficient for one day only, will be purified in one day; he who drinks water given by a person subsisting by the Kapota-v ri tti (pigeon-life), is purified in three (days).

4.5.s: ṛgyajuḥsāmavedānāṃ vedasyānyatamasya vā | pārāyaṇaṃ trir abhyasyed anaśnan so 'tipāvanaḥ |
4.5.d: ऋग्यजुःसामवेदानां वेदस्यान्यतमस्य वा । पारायणं त्रिर् अभ्यस्येद् अनश्नन् सो ऽतिपावनः ।
4.5.e: If one recites the whole Ri g-veda, Ya g ur-veda, and Sāma-veda, or thrice reads one of these Vedas and fasts, (that is) a most efficient means of purification.

4.5.s: atha cet tvarate kartuṃ divasaṃ mārutāśanaḥ | rātrau jalasthito vyuṣṭaḥ prājāpatyena tatsamam |
4.5.d: अथ चेत् त्वरते कर्तुं दिवसं मारुताशनः । रात्रौ जलस्थितो व्युष्टः प्राजापत्येन तत्समम् ।
4.5.e: Now if one is in haste to finish, one may live on air during a day, and pass the night standing in water, that is equal (in efficacy) to a Prā g āpatya (K ri k kh ra).

4.5.s: gāyatryāṣṭasahasraṃ tu japaṃ kṛtvotthite ravau | mucyate sarvapāpebhyo yadi na bhrūṇahā bhavet |
4.5.d: गायत्र्याष्टसहस्रं तु जपं कृत्वोत्थिते रवौ । मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो यदि न भ्रूणहा भवेत् ।
4.5.e: He who at sunrise mutters the Gāyatrī one thousand and eight times, is free from all sin, provided he has not slain a learned Brāhmaṇa.

4.5.s: yo 'nnadaḥ satyavādī ca bhūteṣu kṛpayā sthitaḥ | pūrvoktayantraśuddhebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ so 'tiricyate |
4.5.d: यो ऽन्नदः सत्यवादी च भूतेषु कृपया स्थितः । पूर्वोक्तयन्त्रशुद्धेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः सो ऽतिरिच्यते ।
4.5.e: He who distributes food, speaks the truth, and has compassion on all living beings, is more (holy) than all those who have been purified by the restraints mentioned above.

4.6.s: samādhucchandasā rudrā gāyatrī praṇavānvitā | sapta vyāhṛtayaś caiva japyāḥ pāpavināśanāḥ |
4.6.d: समाधुच्छन्दसा रुद्रा गायत्री प्रणवान्विता । सप्त व्याहृतयश् चैव जप्याः पापविनाशनाः ।
4.6.e: The (eleven Anuvākas called) Rudras together with (the ten hymns) seen by Madhu k kh andas, the Gāyatrī with the syllable Om, and likewise the seven Vyāh ri tis (are the texts) which should be muttered (and) which remove guilt.

4.6.s: mṛgāreṣṭiḥ pavitreṣṭis trihaviḥ pāvamāny api | iṣṭayaḥ pāpanāśinyo vaiśvānaryā samanvitāḥ |
4.6.d: मृगारेष्टिः पवित्रेष्टिस् त्रिहविः पावमान्य् अपि । इष्टयः पापनाशिन्यो वैश्वानर्या समन्विताः ।
4.6.e: The M ri gāreshṭi, the Pavitreshṭi, the Trihavis, the Pāvamānī are the Ishṭis which efface sin, if they are (each) combined with the Vaiśvānara (Dvādaśakapāla).

4.6.s: idaṃ caivāparaṃ guhyam ucyamānaṃ nibodhata | mucyate sarvapāpebhyo mahataḥ pātakād ṛte |
4.6.d: इदं चैवापरं गुह्यम् उच्यमानं निबोधत । मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो महतः पातकाद् ऋते ।

4.6.s: pavitrair mārjanaṃ kurvan rudraikādaśinīṃ japan | pavitrāṇi ghṛtair juhvat prayacchan hemagotilān |
4.6.d: पवित्रैर् मार्जनं कुर्वन् रुद्रैकादशिनीं जपन् । पवित्राणि घृतैर् जुह्वत् प्रयच्छन् हेमगोतिलान् ।

4.6.s: yo 'śnīyād yāvakaṃ pakvaṃ gomūtre saśakṛdrase | sadadhikṣīrasarpiṣke mucyate so 'ṃhasaḥ kṣaṇāt |
4.6.d: यो ऽश्नीयाद् यावकं पक्वं गोमूत्रे सशकृद्रसे । सदधिक्षीरसर्पिष्के मुच्यते सो ऽंहसः क्षणात् ।
4.6.e: He who partakes of boiled barley-gruel, mixed with cow's urine, liquid cowdung, sour milk, milk, and butter, is quickly freed from sin.

4.6.s: prasūto yaś ca śūdrāyāṃ yenāgamyā ca laṅghitā | saptarātrāt pramucyete vidhinaitena tāv ubhau |
4.6.d: प्रसूतो यश् च शूद्रायां येनागम्या च लङ्घिता । सप्तरात्रात् प्रमुच्येते विधिनैतेन ताव् उभौ ।
4.6.e: Both he who has begotten a child on a Śūdra woman and he who has had connexion with a female, intercourse with whom is forbidden (agamyā), are purified (if they live) according to this rule during seven days.

4.6.s: retomūtrapurīṣāṇāṃ prāśane 'bhojyabhojane | paryādhānejyayor etat parivitte ca bheṣajam |
4.6.d: रेतोमूत्रपुरीषाणां प्राशने ऽभोज्यभोजने । पर्याधानेज्ययोर् एतत् परिवित्ते च भेषजम् ।
4.6.e: (That is likewise) the remedy when one has swallowed semen, ordure, and urine, or eaten the food of persons whose food must not be eaten, (and also) when a younger brother has kindled the sacred fire, has offered a Śrauta sacrifice, or taken a wife before the elder.

4.6.s: apātakāni karmāṇi kṛtvaiva subahūny api | mucyate sarvapāpebhya ity etad vacanaṃ satām |
4.6.d: अपातकानि कर्माणि कृत्वैव सुबहून्य् अपि । मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्य इत्य् एतद् वचनं सताम् ।
4.6.e: He who has committed even a great number of (wicked) actions, excepting mortal sins, will be freed (by that rule) from all guilt. That is the statement of the virtuous.

4.6.s: mantramārgapramāṇaṃ tu vidhānaṃ samudīritam | bharadvājādayo yena brahmaṇaḥ sātmatāṃ gatāḥ |
4.6.d: मन्त्रमार्गप्रमाणं तु विधानं समुदीरितम् । भरद्वाजादयो येन ब्रह्मणः सात्मतां गताः ।
4.6.e: But (this) ordinance, which is based on the authority of the sacred texts, is stated (to be that) through which Bharadvā g a and others became equal to Brahman,

4.6.s: prasannahṛdayo vipraḥ prayogād asya karmaṇaḥ | kāmāṃs tāṃs tān avāpnoti ye ye kāmā hṛdi sthitāḥ | ye ye kāmā hṛdi sthitā iti |
4.6.d: प्रसन्नहृदयो विप्रः प्रयोगाद् अस्य कर्मणः । कामांस् तांस् तान् अवाप्नोति ये ये कामा हृदि स्थिताः । ये ये कामा हृदि स्थिता इति ।
4.6.e: Through the performance of these rites a Brāhmaṇa, whose heart is full of peace, obtains whatever desires he may have in his heart.

4.7.s: nivṛttaḥ pāpakarmabhyaḥ pravṛttaḥ puṇyakarmasu | yo vipras tasya sidhyanti vinā yantrair api kriyāḥ |
4.7.d: निवृत्तः पापकर्मभ्यः प्रवृत्तः पुण्यकर्मसु । यो विप्रस् तस्य सिध्यन्ति विना यन्त्रैर् अपि क्रियाः ।
4.7.e: The wishes of a Brāhmaṇa who has left off evil deeds and is (ever) engaged in holy works are fulfilled even without (the practice of) restraints.

4.7.s: brāhmaṇā ṛjavas tasmād yad yad icchanti cetasā | tat tad āsādayanty āśu saṃśuddhā ṛjukarmabhiḥ |
4.7.d: ब्राह्मणा ऋजवस् तस्माद् यद् यद् इच्छन्ति चेतसा । तत् तद् आसादयन्त्य् आशु संशुद्धा ऋजुकर्मभिः ।
4.7.e: Upright Brāhmaṇas quickly accomplish whatever they wish in their hearts, if they are purified by honest actions.

4.7.s: evam etāni yantrāṇi tāvat kāryāṇi dhīmatā | kālena yāvatopaiti vigrahaḥ śuddhim ātmanaḥ |
4.7.d: एवम् एतानि यन्त्राणि तावत् कार्याणि धीमता । कालेन यावतोपैति विग्रहः शुद्धिम् आत्मनः ।
4.7.e: Thus a wise man should practise those restraints until he has purified his bodily frame.

4.7.s: ebhir yantrair viśuddhātmā trirātropoṣitas tataḥ | tad ārabheta yenarddhiṃ karmaṇā prāptum icchati |
4.7.d: एभिर् यन्त्रैर् विशुद्धात्मा त्रिरात्रोपोषितस् ततः । तद् आरभेत येनर्द्धिं कर्मणा प्राप्तुम् इच्छति ।
4.7.e: He who has been purified by those restraints should, after fasting three (days and) nights, begin the performance of that sacred rite through which he wishes to gain the fulfilment of his desires,

4.7.s: kṣmāpavitraḥ sahasrākṣo mṛgāro 'ṃhomucau gaṇau | pāvamānyaś ca kūśmāṇḍyo vaiśvānarya ṛcaś ca yāḥ |
4.7.d: क्ष्मापवित्रः सहस्राक्षो मृगारो ऽंहोमुचौ गणौ । पावमान्यश् च कूश्माण्ड्यो वैश्वानर्य ऋचश् च याः ।
4.7.e: (Reciting) the Kshāpavitra, the Sahasrāksha, the M ri gāra, the two G aṇas (called) Aṃhomu k , the Pāvamanīs, the Kūshmāṇd īs, and the Ri k as, addressed to Vaiśvānara,

4.7.s: ghṛtaudanena tā juhvat saptāhaṃ savanatrayam | maunavratī haviṣyāśī nigṛhītendriyakriyaḥ |
4.7.d: घृतौदनेन ता जुह्वत् सप्ताहं सवनत्रयम् । मौनव्रती हविष्याशी निगृहीतेन्द्रियक्रियः ।
4.7.e: (And) offering with (each of) these (Mantras) boiled rice and clarified butter during seven days, in the morning, at midday, and in the evening, keeping a rigid silence, living on food fit for a sacrifice, restraining his senses and his actions,

4.7.s: siṃhe ma ity apāṃ pūrṇe pātre 'vekṣya catuṣpathe | mucyate sarvapāpebhyo mahataḥ pātakād api |
4.7.d: सिंहे म इत्य् अपां पूर्णे पात्रे ऽवेक्ष्य चतुष्पथे । मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो महतः पातकाद् अपि ।
4.7.e: He is freed from all crimes, even mortal sins, after looking on a cross-road at a pot filled with water, (and reciting the text), 'Siṃhe me manyu h .'

4.7.s: vṛddhatve yauvane bālye yaḥ kṛtaḥ pāpasaṃcayaḥ | pūrvajanmasu cājñānāt tasmād api vimucyate |
4.7.d: वृद्धत्वे यौवने बाल्ये यः कृतः पापसंचयः । पूर्वजन्मसु चाज्ञानात् तस्माद् अपि विमुच्यते ।
4.7.e: He is freed from the multitude of sins, committed unintentionally in old age, in youth, and in infancy, and even from those belonging to former births;

4.7.s: bhojayitvā dvijān ante pāyasena sasarpiṣā | gobhūmitilahemāni bhuktavadbhyaḥ pradāya ca |
4.7.d: भोजयित्वा द्विजान् अन्ते पायसेन ससर्पिषा । गोभूमितिलहेमानि भुक्तवद्भ्यः प्रदाय च ।
4.7.e: After feeding at the end (of the seven days) Brāhmaṇas with milk and rice, well. mixed with butter, and distributing to them after their dinner cows, land, sesamum, and gold,

4.7.s: vipro bhavati pūtātmā nirdagdhavṛjinendhanaḥ | kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ yogyas tathādhānādikarmaṇām |
4.7.d: विप्रो भवति पूतात्मा निर्दग्धवृजिनेन्धनः । काम्यानां कर्मणां योग्यस् तथाधानादिकर्मणाम् ।
4.7.e: A Brāhmaṇa becomes internally pure, his guilt being consumed like fuel, and fit for the performance of rites which secure the fulfilment of wishes and of rites like the kindling of the sacred fire.

4.8.s: atilobhāt pramādād vā yaḥ karoti kriyām imām | anyasya so 'ṃha āviṣṭo garagīr iva sīdati |
4.8.d: अतिलोभात् प्रमादाद् वा यः करोति क्रियाम् इमाम् । अन्यस्य सो ऽंह आविष्टो गरगीर् इव सीदति ।
4.8.e: He who, through excessive greed or carelessness, performs this rite for others, is tainted by sin, and perishes like one who has swallowed poison.

4.8.s: ācāryasya pitur mātur ātmanaś ca kriyām imām | kurvan bhāty arkavad vipraḥ sā kāryaiṣām ataḥ kriyā |
4.8.d: आचार्यस्य पितुर् मातुर् आत्मनश् च क्रियाम् इमाम् । कुर्वन् भात्य् अर्कवद् विप्रः सा कार्यैषाम् अतः क्रिया ।
4.8.e: A Brāhmaṇa who performs this rite for his teacher, his father, his mother, or for himself is resplendent like the sun. Therefore this rite may be performed for those (persons).

4.8.s: ka etena sahasrākṣaṃ pavitreṇākaroc chucim | agniṃ vāyuṃ raviṃ somaṃ yamādīṃś ca sureśvarān |
4.8.d: क एतेन सहस्राक्षं पवित्रेणाकरोच् छुचिम् । अग्निं वायुं रविं सोमं यमादींश् च सुरेश्वरान् ।
4.8.e: Ka (Pra g āpati) purified by means of this rite the god with a thousand eyes (Sahasrāksha), Fire, Wind, the Sun, Soma, Yama, and other lords of the gods.

4.8.s: yat kiṃcit puṇyanāmeha triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam | viprādi tat kṛtaṃ kena pavitrakriyayānayā |
4.8.d: यत् किंचित् पुण्यनामेह त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम् । विप्रादि तत् कृतं केन पवित्रक्रिययानया ।
4.8.e: Whatever there is in these three worlds, famed as possessing a holy name, Brāhmaṇas and the rest, (all) that was produced by Ka through this rite of sanctification.

4.8.s: prājāpatyam idaṃ guhyaṃ pāpaghnaṃprathamodbhavam | samutpannāny ataḥ paścāt pavitrāṇi sahasraśaḥ |
4.8.d: प्राजापत्यम् इदं गुह्यं पापघ्नंप्रथमोद्भवम् । समुत्पन्नान्य् अतः पश्चात् पवित्राणि सहस्रशः ।
4.8.e: This sin-destroying secret of Pra g āpati was first produced; thereafter thousands of purificatory rites .came into existence.

4.8.s: yo 'bdāyanartupakṣāhāñ juhoty aṣṭau gaṇān imān | punāti cātmano vaṃśyān daśa pūrvān daśāvarān |
4.8.d: यो ऽब्दायनर्तुपक्षाहाञ् जुहोत्य् अष्टौ गणान् इमान् । पुनाति चात्मनो वंश्यान् दश पूर्वान् दशावरान् ।
4.8.e: He who performs those eight Gaṇahomas on the (first) day of the year, of a half-year, of a season, or of a fortnight, sanctifies ten ancestors and ten descendants of his line;

4.8.s: jñāyate cāmarair dyusthaiḥ puṇyakarmeti bhūsthitaḥ | devavan modate bhūyaḥ svargaloke 'pi puṇyakṛt |
4.8.d: ज्ञायते चामरैर् द्युस्थैः पुण्यकर्मेति भूस्थितः । देववन् मोदते भूयः स्वर्गलोके ऽपि पुण्यकृत् ।
4.8.e: And, while still on earth, he is known to the gods in heaven as a holy man, and (after death) that virtuous man rejoices for a very long time in heaven like a god.

4.8.s: etān aṣṭau gaṇān hotuṃ na śaknoti yadi dvijaḥ | eko 'pi tena hotavyo rajas tenāsya naśyati |
4.8.d: एतान् अष्टौ गणान् होतुं न शक्नोति यदि द्विजः । एको ऽपि तेन होतव्यो रजस् तेनास्य नश्यति ।
4.8.e: If a Brāhmaṇa is unable to offer those eight Gaṇahomas, let him offer one; thereby his guilt is effaced.

4.8.s: sūnavo yasya śiṣyā vā juhvaty aṣṭau gaṇān imān | adhyāpanaparikrītair aṃhasaḥ so 'pi mucyate |
4.8.d: सूनवो यस्य शिष्या वा जुह्वत्य् अष्टौ गणान् इमान् । अध्यापनपरिक्रीतैर् अंहसः सो ऽपि मुच्यते ।
4.8.e: He, also, whose sons or pupils offer those eight Gaṇahomas, is freed from his sin which is bought off by his having instructed (them).

4.8.s: dhanenāpi parikrītair ātmapāpajighāṃsayā | hāvanīyā hy aśaktena nāvasādyaḥ śarīradhṛk |
4.8.d: धनेनापि परिक्रीतैर् आत्मपापजिघांसया । हावनीया ह्य् अशक्तेन नावसाद्यः शरीरधृक् ।
4.8.e: Through a desire of removing one's guilt one even may cause (these oblations) to be offered by men who have been engaged for money, in case oneself is unable (to do it); a man need not torment himself.

4.8.s: dhanasya kriyate tyāgaḥ karmaṇāṃ sukṛtām api | puṃso 'nṛṇasya pāpasya vimokṣaḥ kriyate kvacit |
4.8.d: धनस्य क्रियते त्यागः कर्मणां सुकृताम् अपि । पुंसो ऽनृणस्य पापस्य विमोक्षः क्रियते क्वचित् ।
4.8.e: Even among the virtuous a distribution of wealth is made (for the success) of holy rites; some-times a man who is free from debt is (thereby) freed from guilt. 12, Liberated according to this rule from the ocean of guilt and debt, he considers himself pure and able to successfully perform the sacred rites.

4.8.s: vimukto vidhinaitena sarvapāpārṇasāgarāt | ātmānaṃ manyate śuddhaṃ samarthaṃ karmasādhane |
4.8.d: विमुक्तो विधिनैतेन सर्वपापार्णसागरात् । आत्मानं मन्यते शुद्धं समर्थं कर्मसाधने ।

4.8.s: sarvapāpārṇamuktātmā kriyā ārabhate tu yāḥ | ayatnenaiva tāḥ siddhiṃ yānti śuddhaśarīriṇaḥ |
4.8.d: सर्वपापार्णमुक्तात्मा क्रिया आरभते तु याः । अयत्नेनैव ताः सिद्धिं यान्ति शुद्धशरीरिणः ।

4.8.s: prājāpatyam idaṃ puṇyam ṛṣiṇā samudīritam | idam adhyāpayen nityaṃ dhārayec chṛṇute 'pi vā | mucyate sarvapāpebhyo brahmaloke mahīyate |
4.8.d: प्राजापत्यम् इदं पुण्यम् ऋषिणा समुदीरितम् । इदम् अध्यापयेन् नित्यं धारयेच् छृणुते ऽपि वा । मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ।

4.8.s: yān siṣādhayiṣur mantrān dvādaśāhāni tāñ japet | ghṛtena payasā dadhnā prāśya niśy odanaṃ sakṛt |
4.8.d: यान् सिषाधयिषुर् मन्त्रान् द्वादशाहानि ताञ् जपेत् । घृतेन पयसा दध्ना प्राश्य निश्य् ओदनं सकृत् ।

4.8.s: daśavāraṃ tathā homaḥ sarpiṣā savanatrayam | pūrvasevā bhaved eṣāṃ mantrāṇāṃ karmasādhane | mantrāṇāṃ karmasādhana iti || atilobhāt pramādād vā | nivṛttaḥ pāpakarmabhyaḥ || samādhuśchandasārudrāḥ || athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi || prāyaścittāni vakṣyāmaḥ || prāyaścittāni vakṣyāmaḥ || prāyaścittāni vakṣyāmaḥ || prāyaścittānivakṣyāmaḥ || iti caturthaḥ praśnaḥ || iti baudhāyanadharmasūtraṃsamāptam |
4.8.d: दशवारं तथा होमः सर्पिषा सवनत्रयम् । पूर्वसेवा भवेद् एषां मन्त्राणां कर्मसाधने । मन्त्राणां कर्मसाधन इति ॥ अतिलोभात् प्रमादाद् वा । निवृत्तः पापकर्मभ्यः ॥ समाधुश्छन्दसारुद्राः ॥ अथातः संप्रवक्ष्यामि ॥ प्रायश्चित्तानि वक्ष्यामः ॥ प्रायश्चित्तानि वक्ष्यामः ॥ प्रायश्चित्तानि वक्ष्यामः ॥ प्रायश्चित्तानिवक्ष्यामः ॥ इति चतुर्थः प्रश्नः ॥ इति बौधायनधर्मसूत्रंसमाप्तम् ।
